We're Searching for Our Next Chief Operating Officer

Not simply to manage a law firm. But to help continue building one of the most innovative family law firms in the country.

Laughlin Legal, PC represents founders, venture capital professionals, technology executives, entrepreneurs, physicians, professional athletes, and other sophisticated clients throughout Silicon Valley and California. Our matters frequently involve complex financial issues, executive compensation, founder equity, private equity, closely held businesses, international issues, and high-conflict custody litigation.

Over the past thirteen years, we have built one of California's fastest-growing family law firms. Our gross revenue has increased by approximately 25% to 50% year over year for thirteen consecutive years.

Why? Because we are relentless in our pursuit of excellence. We strive to provide the highest level of legal representation and client service in family law in California. We invest in exceptional people, embrace innovation, continually refine our systems, and refuse to become complacent. We believe that when you build an extraordinary team and deliver an extraordinary client experience, sustained growth naturally follows.

Just as importantly, we believe extraordinary results should never come at the expense of extraordinary people.

We have intentionally built a collaborative, collegial culture where people genuinely enjoy working together, support one another, and are committed to each other's success. We value excellence, but we also value balance. Unlike many firms, our attorneys are expected to bill only 1,400 hours per year, allowing them to spend meaningful time with their families, pursue personal interests, and build fulfilling lives outside the office.

We reject the notion that burnout is the price of success. Our experience has proven otherwise. By investing in exceptional people, creating outstanding systems, embracing innovation, and fostering a culture people are proud to be part of, we have achieved remarkable growth while maintaining a workplace where talented professionals choose to build long-term careers.

This is a true executive leadership position. You will serve as my strategic partner in shaping the future of the firm while leading our operations, people, technology, and long-term growth. You will have a meaningful voice in the future direction of the firm and the opportunity to help build an organization that sets a new standard for family law.

Key Responsibilites:
Executive leadership and strategic planning
Recruiting, retaining, and developing exceptional attorneys and professional staff
Associate coaching, mentoring, leadership development, and performance management
Elevating every aspect of the client experience
Optimizing Clio and leveraging its full capabilities across the firm
Designing scalable systems, workflows, and operational excellence
Leading the implementation of artificial intelligence and automation throughout the firm
Coordinating marketing and business development initiatives
Financial management, budgeting, billing, collections, profitability, and key performance metrics
Developing and implementing strategic growth and expansion initiatives
Helping design the firm's future leadership and partnership structure

The Ideal Candidate Will Have:
Significant executive leadership experience within a successful law firm for a minimum of 5 years
Demonstrated success building high-performing teams and scalable operations
Extensive experience with Clio (Clio Certified Consultant or Clio Partner experience is strongly preferred)
Exceptional financial, operational, and business acumen
Experience implementing technology and AI solutions to improve efficiency and client service
Outstanding emotional intelligence, leadership, judgment, and communication skills
An entrepreneurial mindset with an unwavering commitment to excellence
A passion for building organizations, developing people, and creating a culture where others thrive
Excellent references and longevity in employment

We are building more than a successful law firm.

We are building a place where exceptional professionals can do the best work of their careers without sacrificing the people and experiences that matter most. We believe a law firm can be both extraordinarily successful and deeply human. We believe innovation, kindness, accountability, and excellence can coexist. After thirteen years of sustained growth, we have demonstrated that they do.

If our next chapter excites you, we'd love to meet you.

Compensation
Base salary: $260,000–$300,000, depending on experience
Performance bonus
Comprehensive benefits (health, dental, vision, 401-k, life insurance)
3 weeks’ vacation
13 paid holidays
Sick leave

About Jetty Extracts:

Jetty Extracts is a premier cannabis extraction company that produces innovative products and world-class cannabis oils, headquartered in Oakland, CA. In 2013, Jetty Extracts began producing extracts and concentrates in San Diego, CA. Jetty is now one of the top extracts and concentrates brands in California.

Starting with a few individuals committed to creating clean, refined cannabis concentrates by the beach, Jetty has evolved into a group of passionate professionals committed to becoming one of the world’s most respected cannabis brands.

While the last several years have seen Jetty grow exponentially, we continue to be committed to craft, working with small farmers, producing the cleanest and tastiest products, and contributing to our communities. As we do so, we continue to support the Shelter Project, the company’s in-house compassion program that has been providing free cannabis oil to cancer patients since 2014.

About the Role:

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the executive leader responsible for Jetty's manufacturing, supply chain, and operational strategy, ensuring the company has the capabilities, systems, and leadership required to achieve its long-term business objectives.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the COO provides strategic leadership across Jetty's manufacturing network, including production facilities in Oakland, CA and Albany, NY, as well as the company's third-party manufacturing partner in Denver, CO.

The COO is accountable for ensuring the organization's operational capabilities, manufacturing infrastructure, innovation engine, and supply chain network support Jetty's long-term growth, profitability, product quality, and customer commitments. This leader establishes the operational vision, develops organizational capability, and drives enterprise-wide initiatives that improve manufacturing performance, supply chain resilience, capital efficiency, and execution across the network.

As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the COO partners with the CEO and executive leaders to shape company strategy, advise on operational investments, and ensure manufacturing capabilities support Jetty's long-term business objectives.

Key Responsibilities:

Manufacturing Strategy & Operational Leadership: Provide executive leadership for Jetty's manufacturing network while ensuring operational excellence, scalability, and long-term competitiveness.

Establish and execute the company's manufacturing and operations strategy in alignment with corporate objectives.
Lead operational performance across Jetty's manufacturing facilities and third-party manufacturing partnerships.
Build a scalable operating model capable of supporting future growth, geographic expansion, and product innovation.
Drive enterprise-wide operational excellence initiatives that improve efficiency, quality, service, and profitability.
Ensure manufacturing capabilities remain aligned with commercial demand and strategic priorities.
Buildout and Relocation of CA Headquarters: lead the planned relocation of Jetty’s headquarters within California:
Support the executive team in evaluating options that will better suit the growth plan for Jetty in California.
Assist in the design and custom buildout of the space.
Plan and oversee the relocation of all operations, while ensuring inventory remains healthy and minimizing operational hiccups.
Ensure a successful winding down of operations at the current facility.

Innovation, R&D & Scale-Up: Build and institutionalize a scalable innovation, research & development, and commercialization engine that supports Jetty's long-term growth, product leadership, and market expansion.

Establish the strategic vision, structure, and operating model for Jetty's innovation, R&D, and commercialization functions.
Develop a stage-gate innovation process that enables efficient product development, testing, commercialization, and continuous improvement.
Create a repeatable framework for evaluating, prioritizing, and advancing innovation opportunities from concept through market launch.
Partner with Product, Marketing, Strategy, Sales, and Manufacturing teams to translate consumer insights and business priorities into a robust innovation pipeline.
Evaluate current manufacturing processes, equipment, and throughput to identify opportunities for innovation, automation, and scalability.
Build the systems, talent, and capabilities required to support new product development, formulation innovation, process improvement, and technology evaluation.
Develop and manage capital and operating plans required to scale manufacturing capabilities in support of future market expansion.
Work with internal teams and external partners to design, develop, test, and implement new equipment, technologies, and production processes.
Ensure successful scale-up and commercialization of new products and processes from concept through full production while maintaining quality, compliance, and operational efficiency.
Establish innovation and R&D performance metrics, resource planning, and prioritization frameworks that maximize return on investment.
Foster a culture of experimentation, learning, and continuous improvement that strengthens Jetty's competitive advantage and supports future market expansion.

Supply Chain & Network Optimization: Develop a resilient, efficient manufacturing network that delivers consistent execution and supports long-term business growth.

Provide executive oversight of production planning, procurement, inventory strategy, logistics, and manufacturing partnerships.
Optimize manufacturing capacity, network utilization, and supply chain performance across all operating locations.
Develop long-term capacity and capital planning strategies to support future growth.
Strengthen strategic relationships with key suppliers and manufacturing partners to improve operational resilience.

Financial Stewardship: Drive operational performance that strengthens profitability and creates long-term enterprise value.

Own manufacturing and operations financial performance, including operating budgets, capital investments, and productivity initiatives.
Identify opportunities to improve gross margin through operational efficiency, manufacturing optimization, and disciplined resource allocation.
Establish operational performance metrics that provide executive visibility into business health and manufacturing effectiveness.
Partner with Finance on long-range planning, forecasting, and investment decisions.

Operational Governance, Quality & Compliance: Ensure operational integrity through disciplined governance, quality systems, and regulatory excellence.

Champion operational governance that ensures consistent execution across all manufacturing locations.
Maintain the highest standards of quality, compliance, product safety, and regulatory adherence.
Establish enterprise-wide operating standards and accountability for operational performance.
Proactively identify operational risks and implement strategies that strengthen business continuity.

Executive Leadership & Organizational Development: Build an operational organization capable of sustaining high performance and long-term growth.

Lead and develop the senior operations organization, including the Vice President of Operations, site leaders, supply chain functions, and innovation/R&D capabilities.
Build organizational capability through leadership development, succession planning, and talent strategies that position Jetty for long-term growth.
Partner with the Head of People to strengthen organizational design, workforce planning, and employee development across the manufacturing organization.
Serve as a trusted member of the Executive Leadership Team, providing strategic guidance on operational performance, organizational capability, and business growth.

Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business Administration, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing, operations, or supply chain, including executive-level responsibility for multi-site operations.
Proven success leading complex manufacturing organizations through periods of growth, transformation, and operational scaling.
Demonstrated experience overseeing multiple production facilities and/or contract manufacturing partnerships within a regulated industry.
Experience leading innovation, product commercialization, process scale-up, or R&D functions within a manufacturing environment.
Strong financial acumen with experience managing operating budgets, capital investments, cost optimization, and operational profitability.
Track record of building high-performing leadership teams and developing operational talent through coaching, succession planning, and organizational development.
Experience driving Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, operational excellence, and change management initiatives.
Strong understanding of production planning, quality systems, inventory management, supply chain strategy, and manufacturing network optimization.
Exceptional executive communication, strategic thinking, and cross-functional leadership skills, with the ability to influence at the executive and Board levels.
Experience in cannabis, consumer packaged goods (CPG), food and beverage, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments strongly preferred.

What Success Looks Like in 12 Months:

Manufacturing operations across Oakland, Albany, and Jetty's Denver manufacturing partner operate with greater consistency, accountability, and alignment under a unified operational strategy.

JK Executive Strategies is proud to partner with the Board of Directors of Jordan Health in search of its next President & CEO. Founded in 1904, Jordan Health is one of the nation's oldest Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) and a recognized leader in providing comprehensive, community-based healthcare services throughout the Greater Rochester region. The organization delivers primary care, dental, behavioral health, women’s health, pediatrics, pharmacy, urgent care, and specialty services to nearly 30,000 patients annually.

The President & CEO serves as the strategic and operational leader of Jordan Health, responsible for advancing the organization’s mission while ensuring clinical excellence, financial sustainability, regulatory compliance, workforce engagement, and organizational effectiveness. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO provides vision, leadership, and accountability for all aspects of organizational performance.

Jordan Health seeks a transformational executive to lead the organization through a critical period of financial stabilization, operational improvement, and strategic growth. The successful candidate will bring executive leadership experience within an FQHC, community health center, safety-net healthcare organization, or similarly complex healthcare environment. This leader will possess expertise in healthcare reimbursement, regulatory compliance, operational excellence, workforce development, and community-centered care.
The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated track record of improving financial performance, strengthening revenue cycle operations, building high-performing teams, and leading organizations through significant change while fostering a culture of accountability, transparency, and service excellence.

• Partner with the Board of Directors to establish organizational strategy, priorities, and long-term sustainability plans.

• Assess emerging risks, opportunities, and community needs to guide strategic decision-making and service expansion.

• Represent Jordan Health with healthcare partners, government agencies, advocacy organizations, funders, and community stakeholders.

• Provide leadership and oversight for budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and resource allocation.

• Monitor key financial indicators and implement strategies that improve financial performance while maintaining mission alignment.
• Ensure strong financial controls, audit readiness, and compliance with grant and funding requirements.
Operational Excellence & Compliance

• Ensure delivery of high-quality, accessible, patient-centered services that meet community needs and FQHC requirements.
• Promote continuous improvement through quality initiatives, operational efficiencies, and performance management systems.
• Oversee organizational infrastructure, facilities, technology, and resources necessary to support current operations and future growth.
• Ensure compliance with HRSA requirements, FQHC regulations, federal and state laws, accreditation standards, and reporting requirements.
• Oversee enterprise risk management activities that promote organizational integrity, accountability, and regulatory compliance.
Leadership & Workforce Development

• Build, develop, and retain a high-performing executive leadership team aligned around accountability, collaboration, and service excellence.
• Foster a culture of trust, transparency, inclusion, employee engagement, and continuous improvement.
• Lead workforce recruitment, retention, succession planning, and leadership development initiatives.
• Recruit and retain high-quality providers, clinical staff, and operational leaders while developing future organizational leaders.
Community Leadership

• Serve as a visible and trusted leader within the Rochester community and broader healthcare ecosystem.
• Engage patients, employees, community partners, funders, and elected officials in advancing organizational priorities and health equity.
• Ensure community and patient voices are incorporated into organizational planning and decision-making.
• Support fundraising, grant development, marketing, communications, and community outreach efforts that strengthen organizational sustainability and reputation.
CORE COMPETENCIES

• FQHC Leadership
• Financial Turnaround & Stabilization
• Healthcare Reimbursement & Revenue Cycle Strategy
• HRSA Compliance & Governance
• Organizational Transformation & Change Management
• Workforce Development & Retention
• Board Relations & Community Engagement
• Health Equity & Risk Management

• Minimum of ten (10) years of progressive executive leadership experience, including substantial leadership responsibility within an FQHC, community health center, safety-net healthcare organization, or similarly regulated healthcare environment. Direct FQHC experience strongly preferred.

jobs.description:
Job Opening: Executive Director

About Philo Ridge Farm:

Philo Ridge Farm (PRF) is a certified organic 500-acre farm located in Charlotte, Vermont, a vibrant agricultural community in the Champlain Valley, just south of Burlington. As a diversified farm with a decade of production experience, PRF aims to create a new model for small-scale farmers, one that will allow both the land and the farmer to prosper while also serving the community. PRF works with the University of Vermont, the Vermont Land Trust, and others to help monitor and evaluate its impacts on soil health, crop and pasture productivity, water quality, carbon sequestration, and wildlife populations, with the goal of inspiring others who are interested in understanding and supporting regenerative agriculture.

Creating and sharing good food has always been a part of PRF’s work and spirit—as established by the founders Peter Swift, Diana McCargo, and Grant McCargo—who bought the property with the dream of preserving the farm’s agricultural legacy. PRF’s livestock program grazes over 300 acres of perennial pasture and includes ewes, lambs, pigs, chickens, and 100 Belted Galloway cattle. Its garden program grows two acres of organic produce and flowers using farming practices that build soil health, produce a variety of nutrient-dense foods, reduce the use of fossil fuels, and support the local agricultural community. Everything harvested is processed at PRF and sold in the dining facilities and Market which are inspired by a closed-loop nutrient system and serve as year-round gathering places for the community.

After a decade of learning the land, growing with the community, and envisioning the future of farming, the founders have established PRF as a nonprofit foundation so that the farm continues to operate as a community asset for generations to come. PRF believes a key part of this future is to keep working lands working, which is why it will always remain a working farm. Today, PRF is driven to restore the connection between humans and land, valuing curiosity, empathy, honesty, humility, and conversation.

Who We’re Looking For:

Philo Ridge Farm is looking for an outstanding and inspiring leader to be our Executive Director. The Executive Director will be the top senior leadership position on the farm, which operates year-round with a high season from May to October, and will oversee all aspects of day-to-day operations. This person will be an enthusiastic, entrepreneurial, creative, and hands-on leader of all parts of this diverse and innovative farm, including land-based agriculture teams, the market and events space, food service and hospitality teams, and the produce and meat processing facilities. The Executive Director will oversee all business operations, financial tracking and management, leadership development, internal communication, outward-facing marketing, human resources, and administration. In addition, this person will be the key ambassador for PRF’s core values, mission, and story to the local community as well as to the broader food and agriculture community.

The Executive Director must share PRF’s passion for land conservation, growing produce, raising animals, and how they intersect with food and hospitality. They will provide operational excellence through inspiring leadership, strategic thinking, team development, and a willingness to roll up their sleeves and participate in the hands-on work of the farm when needed, all while providing experienced financial and operational management of the business. Strong candidates will be equally comfortable managing Excel spreadsheets as they are hosing off their muck boots, all while creating a welcoming, community atmosphere across all aspects of the farm. In this role, the Executive Director will be a facilitator, an active listener, a clear communicator, a mentor, a coach, a mediator, and a source of positive inspiration for the entire team at PRF and someone who can motivate and hold staff members accountable to the foundations ethos and goals. The Executive Director will report to the Philo Ridge Farm Foundation Board, will work daily at PRF, and will need to live locally.

Responsibilities:

Strategic Management
Lead the design and development of annual strategic goals and a five-year strategic plan in collaboration with the Board
Adapt and align organizational structures and ways of working as needed to ensure that PRF’s departments, staffing, and budget are aligned with the strategic goals
Lead the development, implementation, and continual refinement of organizational metrics
Maintain regular communication with the Board regarding farm operations and performance
Serve as a steward and model of the farm’s mission, vision, and values
Provide strategic leadership for current and future entities under the PRF Foundation’s umbrella, including Vermont Livestock Slaughter & Processing

Team Management
Effectively recruit, train, coach, and develop managers and staff across departments
Create a positive, inspired team-oriented culture rooted in communication and collaboration
Ensure accountability by actively demonstrating and teaching exceptional professionalism
Support individual managers to facilitate staff learning and development
Hold individual managers accountable to address staff incidents and interpersonal issues
Support Board in the development and implementation of new business units and teams

Operations Management

Summary
The Development Director serves as a key member of the Senior Leadership Team and provides strategic leadership for New Life Center's fundraising, donor and volunteer engagement, and community partnership efforts. Reporting to the Executive Director, this role is responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive fundraising and engagement strategy that generates contributed revenue, deepens supporter engagement, and expands opportunities for individuals, churches, and community partners to engage in the Mission through giving, serving, and prayer.

The Development Director serves as the organization’s chief relationship builder and external ambassador, cultivating connections with major donors, churches, businesses, community leaders, and strategic partners. This role provides leadership and oversight for fundraising initiatives, donor and volunteer engagement strategies, donor and volunteer relationship management systems, and contributed revenue goals. The Development Director leads and develops the development team, coaches fundraising staff, and maintains a select portfolio of major donor relationships. Working closely with the Executive Director, Board of Directors, and Marketing Director, the Development Director ensures fundraising efforts, supporter engagement, and community partnerships effectively advance the organization’s mission and strategic priorities.

The Development Director serves as both a ministry leader and fundraising professional, helping supporters understand and experience the transformational impact of New Life Center’s ministry. Through authentic relationships, compelling vision casting, prayer, and faithful stewardship, this role invites supporters into deeper involvement in the life-transforming work of Jesus Christ among those experiencing homelessness and hardship. The Development Director models Christ-centered leadership while advancing the mission, sustainability, and long-term impact of New Life Center.

Our work is rooted in our Christian faith and driven by our mission to guide people experiencing homelessness or addiction toward holistic transformation through the love of Jesus. Every role contributes to this ministry and advances our shared vision. Our team members are followers of Jesus Christ, affirm our Statement of Faith, and demonstrate our BEACON values.

For more than a decade, we’ve worked to show that with the mindful use of technology, we can break down barriers, meet community needs, and find real solutions.

Our employees build and transform government and community tools and services, making them so good they inspire change. We merge the best parts of technology, nonprofit, and government to help support the people who need it most.

With a focus on transparency and fairness, and deep empathy for partners in government and community organizations and the people that our partners serve, we’re building a movement of motivated change agents driven by meaningful results and lasting impact.

At Code for America, you contribute to exciting work while learning and developing in a supportive and flexible environment. Our compensation and benefits are holistic and thoughtfully curated to represent our employees and our mission. Help us drive real generational change that lasts.

Code for America is looking for a talented Program Director
who will own delivery and strategic direction across a portfolio of high-impact programs. In this role, you will manage a team of Associate Program Directors and program staff, setting the conditions for excellent execution while maintaining the external relationships and policy fluency that government work requires. You will ensure that Code for America's programs not only deliver for clients and partners today, but build the organizational learning, government trust, and policy foundations that enable systemic, lasting change.

About the role:

Code for America's Program Directors lead portfolios of work that sit at the intersection of technology, policy, and government service delivery. At the core of this role is the belief that government services can and should work better for the people who depend on them most — and that achieving that requires sustained, expert leadership over complex, multi-stakeholder programs.

As a Program Director at Code for America, you will own a portfolio of approximately four to six projects and the teams that deliver them. Your portfolio may include work across areas such as Safety Net benefits access (including multi-benefit enrollment and Medicaid and SNAP delivery), Tax programs, or Criminal Justice initiatives, depending on organizational need and your area of expertise.

You will be externally facing, building and sustaining relationships with federal agencies, state-level leadership, county partners, and/or community-based organizations, while supporting your direct reports in doing the same. You will also work closely with other delivery colleagues to ensure our projects achieve their intended impact and that your portfolio is aligned with Code for America's strategy.

This role will report to the Senior Director of Safety Net
and is expected to travel no more than 15%-25% of the time.

Code for America is based in California and can employ those who reside full-time within the United States. This is a remote position.

In this position you will:

Portfolio Oversight
Own partnership escalation and/or strategic direction across a portfolio of approximately four to six projects, ensuring each project meets its commitments to government partners, funders, and clients, and outputs are high-quality and delivered on time and within budget.
Collaborate with the Partnerships team to ensure efficient scoping and smooth handoffs, including clear kickoff processes and well-defined responsibilities during project kickoffs and transitions.
Ensure programs staff apply consistent delivery management practices, focused on setting clear project timelines and goals, clarifying roles, and running appropriate meeting cadences, leveraging Code for America's standard best practices, tools, and processes.
Ensure ongoing project-level direction & strategy aligns with organizational strategy, ensuring your portfolio advances mission priorities and contributes to measurable client outcomes.
Work with programs team members, programs leadership, and discipline leads to ensure each project has a clear, realistic plan for success aligned with organizational goals, partner expectations, client outcomes, and/or philanthropic commitments, and that programs staff understand how to drive aligned progress.
Anticipate risks, staffing needs, and resource constraints across your portfolio; serve as the primary escalation point for APDs and programs staff , escalating to programs leadership when the decision has implications beyond your purview.
Support APDs in driving clear, frequent communication internally and with external stakeholders to maintain alignment on program progress, scope changes, risks, and emerging opportunities.
Partner with programs and resource management leadership to ensure project teams are staffed appropriately from a programs perspective; contribute to headcount recommendations and support recruitment and onboarding of new team members.
Ensure APDs serving as Project Sponsors surface staffing needs across delivery disciplines early and escalate when tradeoffs or reprioritization are required. Proactively flag when teams need resource adjustments to ensure strong delivery across multiple teams.

People Management
Directly manage Associate Program Directors (APDs) and, where applicable, other Program ICs within your portfolio; provide coaching, feedback, and development support that builds their effectiveness as program leaders.
Coach and develop people managers on the team, supporting them in managing their own direct reports effectively.
Lead goal setting, performance reviews, and regular check-ins to support team performance, professional growth, and team culture.
Model Code for America's values and ways of working across your team, setting expectations for how program staff use best practices and tools, engage with partners, clients, and each other, to ensure strong and efficient program delivery across your portfolio

Strategy & Operations
Surface insights from projects and partners to inform organizational priorities, strategy, and emerging opportunities, as well as to identify possibilities for policy and systems change.
Participate in optional cross-functional working groups addressing organizational priorities, emerging program practices, and the role of technology and artificial intelligence in government service delivery, as relevant.
Ensure lessons learned inform other projects across your portfolio and the broader delivery area.

External Relationships & Communications
Build and sustain relationships with federal agency leads, state-level government partners, county agencies, and mission-aligned community-based organizations across your portfolio.
Travel to partner sites, government offices, and program locations as needed to maintain trust, assess project health, and identify opportunities for deeper engagement.
Serve as a credible, knowledgeable voice for Code for America for work within your purview, representing the organization's work you oversee and approach with government and funder audiences.
Contribute to cultivation efforts within your portfolio area, including opportunity spotting, advising on statements of work, project scoping, and pitch materials in partnership with the Growth and Partnerships team.
Ensure reporting across projects is purposeful, consistent, and aligned with funder and partner requirements, surfacing the right insights and signals for internal organizational leadership. This may include drafting, reviewing, and/or approving grant reports for projects in your portfolio.

Other duties as assigned
Engage in ad hoc projects and initiatives as required by the organization's evolving needs.

About you:

8+ years of experience in program development, policy, or government service delivery, with demonstrated progression of responsibility; some experience working within or directly alongside government required.
Familiarity with agile or iterative program delivery approaches, and experience collaborating with product and engineering teams.
3+ years of experience managing teams, including direct management of at least one people manager.
Proven track record of owning complex, multi-stakeholder program delivery — from strategy through execution — in a government, civic tech, or social sector context.
Deep familiarity with at least one of Code for America's program areas: Safety Net benefits access (including SNAP, Medicaid, or multi-benefit enrollment), Tax programs, or Criminal Justice; ability to credibly represent Code for America's approach with government partners in that area.
Demonstrated ability to build and sustain trusted relationships with federal and state agency leadership, county partners, and community-based organizations across political and institutional differences.
Strong understanding of government service delivery structures, including the social safety net, and the policy landscape shaping program implementation.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex program and policy information clearly & concisely to government partners, funders, and internal leadership.

We're Searching for Our Next Chief Operating Officer

Not simply to manage a law firm. But to help continue building one of the most innovative family law firms in the country.

Laughlin Legal, PC represents founders, venture capital professionals, technology executives, entrepreneurs, physicians, professional athletes, and other sophisticated clients throughout Silicon Valley and California. Our matters frequently involve complex financial issues, executive compensation, founder equity, private equity, closely held businesses, international issues, and high-conflict custody litigation.

Over the past thirteen years, we have built one of California's fastest-growing family law firms. Our gross revenue has increased by approximately 25% to 50% year over year for thirteen consecutive years.

Why? Because we are relentless in our pursuit of excellence. We strive to provide the highest level of legal representation and client service in family law in California. We invest in exceptional people, embrace innovation, continually refine our systems, and refuse to become complacent. We believe that when you build an extraordinary team and deliver an extraordinary client experience, sustained growth naturally follows.

Just as importantly, we believe extraordinary results should never come at the expense of extraordinary people.

We have intentionally built a collaborative, collegial culture where people genuinely enjoy working together, support one another, and are committed to each other's success. We value excellence, but we also value balance. Unlike many firms, our attorneys are expected to bill only 1,400 hours per year, allowing them to spend meaningful time with their families, pursue personal interests, and build fulfilling lives outside the office.

We reject the notion that burnout is the price of success. Our experience has proven otherwise. By investing in exceptional people, creating outstanding systems, embracing innovation, and fostering a culture people are proud to be part of, we have achieved remarkable growth while maintaining a workplace where talented professionals choose to build long-term careers.

This is a true executive leadership position. You will serve as my strategic partner in shaping the future of the firm while leading our operations, people, technology, and long-term growth. You will have a meaningful voice in the future direction of the firm and the opportunity to help build an organization that sets a new standard for family law.

Key Responsibilites:
Executive leadership and strategic planning
Recruiting, retaining, and developing exceptional attorneys and professional staff
Associate coaching, mentoring, leadership development, and performance management
Elevating every aspect of the client experience
Optimizing Clio and leveraging its full capabilities across the firm
Designing scalable systems, workflows, and operational excellence
Leading the implementation of artificial intelligence and automation throughout the firm
Coordinating marketing and business development initiatives
Financial management, budgeting, billing, collections, profitability, and key performance metrics
Developing and implementing strategic growth and expansion initiatives
Helping design the firm's future leadership and partnership structure

The Ideal Candidate Will Have:
Significant executive leadership experience within a successful law firm for a minimum of 5 years
Demonstrated success building high-performing teams and scalable operations
Extensive experience with Clio (Clio Certified Consultant or Clio Partner experience is strongly preferred)
Exceptional financial, operational, and business acumen
Experience implementing technology and AI solutions to improve efficiency and client service
Outstanding emotional intelligence, leadership, judgment, and communication skills
An entrepreneurial mindset with an unwavering commitment to excellence
A passion for building organizations, developing people, and creating a culture where others thrive
Excellent references and longevity in employment

We are building more than a successful law firm.

We are building a place where exceptional professionals can do the best work of their careers without sacrificing the people and experiences that matter most. We believe a law firm can be both extraordinarily successful and deeply human. We believe innovation, kindness, accountability, and excellence can coexist. After thirteen years of sustained growth, we have demonstrated that they do.

If our next chapter excites you, we'd love to meet you.

Compensation
Base salary: $260,000–$300,000, depending on experience
Performance bonus
Comprehensive benefits (health, dental, vision, 401-k, life insurance)
3 weeks’ vacation
13 paid holidays
Sick leave

Please send your résumé and a cover letter explaining why this opportunity speaks to you to careers@laughlinlegal.com

They are built by visionary leaders who know how to attract exceptional people, create extraordinary systems, embrace innovation, and build organizations that endure.

About Jetty Extracts:

Jetty Extracts is a premier cannabis extraction company that produces innovative products and world-class cannabis oils, headquartered in Oakland, CA. In 2013, Jetty Extracts began producing extracts and concentrates in San Diego, CA. Jetty is now one of the top extracts and concentrates brands in California.

Starting with a few individuals committed to creating clean, refined cannabis concentrates by the beach, Jetty has evolved into a group of passionate professionals committed to becoming one of the world’s most respected cannabis brands.

While the last several years have seen Jetty grow exponentially, we continue to be committed to craft, working with small farmers, producing the cleanest and tastiest products, and contributing to our communities. As we do so, we continue to support the Shelter Project, the company’s in-house compassion program that has been providing free cannabis oil to cancer patients since 2014.

About the Role:

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the executive leader responsible for Jetty's manufacturing, supply chain, and operational strategy, ensuring the company has the capabilities, systems, and leadership required to achieve its long-term business objectives.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the COO provides strategic leadership across Jetty's manufacturing network, including production facilities in Oakland, CA and Albany, NY, as well as the company's third-party manufacturing partner in Denver, CO.

The COO is accountable for ensuring the organization's operational capabilities, manufacturing infrastructure, innovation engine, and supply chain network support Jetty's long-term growth, profitability, product quality, and customer commitments. This leader establishes the operational vision, develops organizational capability, and drives enterprise-wide initiatives that improve manufacturing performance, supply chain resilience, capital efficiency, and execution across the network.

As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the COO partners with the CEO and executive leaders to shape company strategy, advise on operational investments, and ensure manufacturing capabilities support Jetty's long-term business objectives.

Key Responsibilities:

Manufacturing Strategy & Operational Leadership: Provide executive leadership for Jetty's manufacturing network while ensuring operational excellence, scalability, and long-term competitiveness.

Establish and execute the company's manufacturing and operations strategy in alignment with corporate objectives.
Lead operational performance across Jetty's manufacturing facilities and third-party manufacturing partnerships.
Build a scalable operating model capable of supporting future growth, geographic expansion, and product innovation.
Drive enterprise-wide operational excellence initiatives that improve efficiency, quality, service, and profitability.
Ensure manufacturing capabilities remain aligned with commercial demand and strategic priorities.
Buildout and Relocation of CA Headquarters: lead the planned relocation of Jetty’s headquarters within California:
Support the executive team in evaluating options that will better suit the growth plan for Jetty in California.
Assist in the design and custom buildout of the space.
Plan and oversee the relocation of all operations, while ensuring inventory remains healthy and minimizing operational hiccups.
Ensure a successful winding down of operations at the current facility.

Innovation, R&D & Scale-Up: Build and institutionalize a scalable innovation, research & development, and commercialization engine that supports Jetty's long-term growth, product leadership, and market expansion.

Establish the strategic vision, structure, and operating model for Jetty's innovation, R&D, and commercialization functions.
Develop a stage-gate innovation process that enables efficient product development, testing, commercialization, and continuous improvement.
Create a repeatable framework for evaluating, prioritizing, and advancing innovation opportunities from concept through market launch.
Partner with Product, Marketing, Strategy, Sales, and Manufacturing teams to translate consumer insights and business priorities into a robust innovation pipeline.
Evaluate current manufacturing processes, equipment, and throughput to identify opportunities for innovation, automation, and scalability.
Build the systems, talent, and capabilities required to support new product development, formulation innovation, process improvement, and technology evaluation.
Develop and manage capital and operating plans required to scale manufacturing capabilities in support of future market expansion.
Work with internal teams and external partners to design, develop, test, and implement new equipment, technologies, and production processes.
Ensure successful scale-up and commercialization of new products and processes from concept through full production while maintaining quality, compliance, and operational efficiency.
Establish innovation and R&D performance metrics, resource planning, and prioritization frameworks that maximize return on investment.
Foster a culture of experimentation, learning, and continuous improvement that strengthens Jetty's competitive advantage and supports future market expansion.

Supply Chain & Network Optimization: Develop a resilient, efficient manufacturing network that delivers consistent execution and supports long-term business growth.

Provide executive oversight of production planning, procurement, inventory strategy, logistics, and manufacturing partnerships.
Optimize manufacturing capacity, network utilization, and supply chain performance across all operating locations.
Develop long-term capacity and capital planning strategies to support future growth.
Strengthen strategic relationships with key suppliers and manufacturing partners to improve operational resilience.

Financial Stewardship: Drive operational performance that strengthens profitability and creates long-term enterprise value.

Own manufacturing and operations financial performance, including operating budgets, capital investments, and productivity initiatives.
Identify opportunities to improve gross margin through operational efficiency, manufacturing optimization, and disciplined resource allocation.
Establish operational performance metrics that provide executive visibility into business health and manufacturing effectiveness.
Partner with Finance on long-range planning, forecasting, and investment decisions.

Operational Governance, Quality & Compliance: Ensure operational integrity through disciplined governance, quality systems, and regulatory excellence.

Champion operational governance that ensures consistent execution across all manufacturing locations.
Maintain the highest standards of quality, compliance, product safety, and regulatory adherence.
Establish enterprise-wide operating standards and accountability for operational performance.
Proactively identify operational risks and implement strategies that strengthen business continuity.

Executive Leadership & Organizational Development: Build an operational organization capable of sustaining high performance and long-term growth.

Lead and develop the senior operations organization, including the Vice President of Operations, site leaders, supply chain functions, and innovation/R&D capabilities.
Build organizational capability through leadership development, succession planning, and talent strategies that position Jetty for long-term growth.
Partner with the Head of People to strengthen organizational design, workforce planning, and employee development across the manufacturing organization.
Serve as a trusted member of the Executive Leadership Team, providing strategic guidance on operational performance, organizational capability, and business growth.

Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business Administration, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing, operations, or supply chain, including executive-level responsibility for multi-site operations.
Proven success leading complex manufacturing organizations through periods of growth, transformation, and operational scaling.
Demonstrated experience overseeing multiple production facilities and/or contract manufacturing partnerships within a regulated industry.
Experience leading innovation, product commercialization, process scale-up, or R&D functions within a manufacturing environment.
Strong financial acumen with experience managing operating budgets, capital investments, cost optimization, and operational profitability.
Track record of building high-performing leadership teams and developing operational talent through coaching, succession planning, and organizational development.
Experience driving Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, operational excellence, and change management initiatives.
Strong understanding of production planning, quality systems, inventory management, supply chain strategy, and manufacturing network optimization.
Exceptional executive communication, strategic thinking, and cross-functional leadership skills, with the ability to influence at the executive and Board levels.
Experience in cannabis, consumer packaged goods (CPG), food and beverage, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments strongly preferred.

What Success Looks Like in 12 Months:

Manufacturing operations across Oakland, Albany, and Jetty's Denver manufacturing partner operate with greater consistency, accountability, and alignment under a unified operational strategy.
Operational performance improves across key metrics including productivity, quality, service levels, manufacturing costs, inventory health, and overall equipment effectiveness.
The California headquarters relocation and facility transition are successfully planned and executed, positioning Jetty with a scalable operational footprint while maintaining business continuity, product quality, and customer service levels.
A scalable manufacturing and supply chain strategy is established to support Jetty's long-term growth, innovation pipeline, and commercial objectives.

Executive reporting and operational KPIs provide leadership with clear visibility into manufacturing performance, risks, and opportunities.

A high-performing operations leadership team is developed with clear accountability, strong succession planning, and a culture of continuous improvement, positioning the Vice President of Operations and site leaders for continued growth.

JK Executive Strategies is proud to partner with the Board of Directors of Jordan Health in search of its next President & CEO. Founded in 1904, Jordan Health is one of the nation's oldest Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) and a recognized leader in providing comprehensive, community-based healthcare services throughout the Greater Rochester region. The organization delivers primary care, dental, behavioral health, women’s health, pediatrics, pharmacy, urgent care, and specialty services to nearly 30,000 patients annually.

The President & CEO serves as the strategic and operational leader of Jordan Health, responsible for advancing the organization’s mission while ensuring clinical excellence, financial sustainability, regulatory compliance, workforce engagement, and organizational effectiveness. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO provides vision, leadership, and accountability for all aspects of organizational performance.

Jordan Health seeks a transformational executive to lead the organization through a critical period of financial stabilization, operational improvement, and strategic growth. The successful candidate will bring executive leadership experience within an FQHC, community health center, safety-net healthcare organization, or similarly complex healthcare environment. This leader will possess expertise in healthcare reimbursement, regulatory compliance, operational excellence, workforce development, and community-centered care.
The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated track record of improving financial performance, strengthening revenue cycle operations, building high-performing teams, and leading organizations through significant change while fostering a culture of accountability, transparency, and service excellence.

• Ensure strong financial controls, audit readiness, and compliance with grant and funding requirements.

• Ensure delivery of high-quality, accessible, patient-centered services that meet community needs and FQHC requirements.
• Promote continuous improvement through quality initiatives, operational efficiencies, and performance management systems.
• Oversee organizational infrastructure, facilities, technology, and resources necessary to support current operations and future growth.
• Ensure compliance with HRSA requirements, FQHC regulations, federal and state laws, accreditation standards, and reporting requirements.
• Oversee enterprise risk management activities that promote organizational integrity, accountability, and regulatory compliance.
Leadership & Workforce Development

• Build, develop, and retain a high-performing executive leadership team aligned around accountability, collaboration, and service excellence.
• Foster a culture of trust, transparency, inclusion, employee engagement, and continuous improvement.
• Lead workforce recruitment, retention, succession planning, and leadership development initiatives.
• Recruit and retain high-quality providers, clinical staff, and operational leaders while developing future organizational leaders.
Community Leadership

• Serve as a visible and trusted leader within the Rochester community and broader healthcare ecosystem.
• Engage patients, employees, community partners, funders, and elected officials in advancing organizational priorities and health equity.
• Ensure community and patient voices are incorporated into organizational planning and decision-making.
• Support fundraising, grant development, marketing, communications, and community outreach efforts that strengthen organizational sustainability and reputation.
CORE COMPETENCIES

• FQHC Leadership
• Financial Turnaround & Stabilization
• Healthcare Reimbursement & Revenue Cycle Strategy
• HRSA Compliance & Governance
• Organizational Transformation & Change Management
• Workforce Development & Retention

• Minimum of ten (10) years of progressive executive leadership experience, including substantial leadership responsibility within an FQHC, community health center, safety-net healthcare organization, or similarly regulated healthcare environment. Direct FQHC experience strongly preferred.

Job Opening: Executive Director

About Philo Ridge Farm:

Philo Ridge Farm (PRF) is a certified organic 500-acre farm located in Charlotte, Vermont, a vibrant agricultural community in the Champlain Valley, just south of Burlington. As a diversified farm with a decade of production experience, PRF aims to create a new model for small-scale farmers, one that will allow both the land and the farmer to prosper while also serving the community. PRF works with the University of Vermont, the Vermont Land Trust, and others to help monitor and evaluate its impacts on soil health, crop and pasture productivity, water quality, carbon sequestration, and wildlife populations, with the goal of inspiring others who are interested in understanding and supporting regenerative agriculture.

Creating and sharing good food has always been a part of PRF’s work and spirit—as established by the founders Peter Swift, Diana McCargo, and Grant McCargo—who bought the property with the dream of preserving the farm’s agricultural legacy. PRF’s livestock program grazes over 300 acres of perennial pasture and includes ewes, lambs, pigs, chickens, and 100 Belted Galloway cattle. Its garden program grows two acres of organic produce and flowers using farming practices that build soil health, produce a variety of nutrient-dense foods, reduce the use of fossil fuels, and support the local agricultural community. Everything harvested is processed at PRF and sold in the dining facilities and Market which are inspired by a closed-loop nutrient system and serve as year-round gathering places for the community.

After a decade of learning the land, growing with the community, and envisioning the future of farming, the founders have established PRF as a nonprofit foundation so that the farm continues to operate as a community asset for generations to come. PRF believes a key part of this future is to keep working lands working, which is why it will always remain a working farm. Today, PRF is driven to restore the connection between humans and land, valuing curiosity, empathy, honesty, humility, and conversation.

Who We’re Looking For:

Philo Ridge Farm is looking for an outstanding and inspiring leader to be our Executive Director. The Executive Director will be the top senior leadership position on the farm, which operates year-round with a high season from May to October, and will oversee all aspects of day-to-day operations. This person will be an enthusiastic, entrepreneurial, creative, and hands-on leader of all parts of this diverse and innovative farm, including land-based agriculture teams, the market and events space, food service and hospitality teams, and the produce and meat processing facilities. The Executive Director will oversee all business operations, financial tracking and management, leadership development, internal communication, outward-facing marketing, human resources, and administration. In addition, this person will be the key ambassador for PRF’s core values, mission, and story to the local community as well as to the broader food and agriculture community.

The Executive Director must share PRF’s passion for land conservation, growing produce, raising animals, and how they intersect with food and hospitality. They will provide operational excellence through inspiring leadership, strategic thinking, team development, and a willingness to roll up their sleeves and participate in the hands-on work of the farm when needed, all while providing experienced financial and operational management of the business. Strong candidates will be equally comfortable managing Excel spreadsheets as they are hosing off their muck boots, all while creating a welcoming, community atmosphere across all aspects of the farm. In this role, the Executive Director will be a facilitator, an active listener, a clear communicator, a mentor, a coach, a mediator, and a source of positive inspiration for the entire team at PRF and someone who can motivate and hold staff members accountable to the foundations ethos and goals. The Executive Director will report to the Philo Ridge Farm Foundation Board, will work daily at PRF, and will need to live locally.

Responsibilities:

Strategic Management
Lead the design and development of annual strategic goals and a five-year strategic plan in collaboration with the Board
Adapt and align organizational structures and ways of working as needed to ensure that PRF’s departments, staffing, and budget are aligned with the strategic goals
Lead the development, implementation, and continual refinement of organizational metrics
Maintain regular communication with the Board regarding farm operations and performance
Serve as a steward and model of the farm’s mission, vision, and values
Provide strategic leadership for current and future entities under the PRF Foundation’s umbrella, including Vermont Livestock Slaughter & Processing

Team Management
Effectively recruit, train, coach, and develop managers and staff across departments
Create a positive, inspired team-oriented culture rooted in communication and collaboration
Ensure accountability by actively demonstrating and teaching exceptional professionalism
Support individual managers to facilitate staff learning and development
Hold individual managers accountable to address staff incidents and interpersonal issues
